title: CircleCI vs GitLab CI/CD for solo developers: a technical decision guide
meta_description: Compare CircleCI and GitLab CI/CD for solo developers across architecture, operations, workflow fit, and practical adoption trade-offs using official documentation.
intro: This comparison examines CircleCI and GitLab CI/CD for solo developers. The decision lens is low setup overhead and a small maintenance burden. It uses the maintained catalog and each project's official documentation to separate architectural differences from implementation details that should be verified before adoption.
verdict: Start with CircleCI when its documented model and strongest fit align with a workflow one developer can operate reliably. Prefer GitLab CI/CD when its operating model better matches that requirement. Validate the shortlist with a workload-specific proof of concept before committing production data or delivery pipelines.

faq.question: Which is easier to evaluate first for solo developers?
faq.answer: Begin with the option whose operating model already matches low setup overhead and a small maintenance burden. Use a small proof of concept with the same deployment constraints, team access, and failure modes expected in production.

faq.question: Can CircleCI and GitLab CI/CD be tested with the same benchmark?
faq.answer: Only partly. Measure shared outcomes such as setup time, reliability, maintenance effort, and task completion, then add product-specific checks because the two options can expose different architectural boundaries.

faq.question: What should be verified before making the final choice?
faq.answer: Confirm current support policies, security controls, deployment requirements, integration limits, and upgrade procedures in the official documentation. Recheck any time-sensitive limits immediately before adoption.
